ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: 2-day history of constant dull ache in lower abdomen (below umbilicus) with associated nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.
• Symptoms:
  – Onset/duration: Gradual over the last 2-3 days.
  – Character: Constant dull ache, makes her feel nauseated; no actual vomiting.
  – Constitutional: Subjective fever (hot/sweaty); no light-headedness.
  – GI/urinary: Previously constipated 1 week ago (now resolved, regular BM yesterday). Increased urinary frequency but no dysuria, urgency, foul smell or haematuria. No diarrhoea.
  – Gynaecologic: Last menstrual period ~3 weeks ago; expects next period soon. Mild pink spotting over last couple of days. Sexually active with one partner. Uses etonogestrel implant (Implanon). No vaginal discharge. Unsure about pregnancy.
• Past medical history: None reported.
• Medications: Etonogestrel implant only.
• Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
• Family history: Brother with type 1 diabetes; otherwise non-contributory.
• Social history: Non-smoker, lives with boyfriend.
• Vital signs / exam: Tele-consult only – no vitals, no physical exam performed.
• Labs / imaging: None to date.

V: Ovarian torsion: Sudden lower-abdominal pain and nausea possible; must consider vascular compromise of ovary although pain often acute rather than gradual.
Mesenteric/ovarian vein thrombosis (rare): Pelvic pain + low-grade fever could occur, but little supporting data.
I: Urinary tract infection (cystitis/early pyelonephritis): Lower abdominal discomfort, urinary frequency, subjective fever, nausea.
Pelvic inflammatory disease: Sexually active; lower-abdominal pain, spotting, systemic symptoms.
Appendicitis (early): Periumbilical/lower-abdominal ache with nausea and low-grade fever.
N: Ovarian cyst (with hemorrhage/rupture): Can cause constant pelvic ache and spotting.
Pregnancy-related trophoblastic disease (very unlikely but could give pain/bleeding).
D: Constipation/irritable bowel syndrome: Prior constipation, abdominal ache, but GI symptoms now minimal.
I2: Hormonal implant side-effect: Irregular spotting and mild pelvic discomfort can occur.
Medication-induced gastritis/ulcer – not on NSAIDs or others.
C: Congenital urinary tract anomaly predisposing to infection (indirect).
A: Endometriosis (inflammatory/autoimmune-like): Chronic pelvic pain and spotting, but onset too acute.
T: Minor unnoticed abdominal trauma/strain – no history reported.
E: Early intra-uterine pregnancy or ectopic pregnancy: Pelvic pain, nausea, spotting close to expected menses despite contraception.
Diabetic ketoacidosis – no diabetes, normal urination, so unlikely.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Combination of lower-abdominal discomfort, increased urinary frequency, subjective fever and nausea fits uncomplicated cystitis; absence of dysuria does not exclude it.
opposing_evidence: No dysuria or suprapubic tenderness documented
Mild pink tinge may represent vaginal rather than urinary blood

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Sexually active female of reproductive age with spotting near expected menses, nausea and pelvic pain; implant lowers but does not eliminate pregnancy risk; ectopic must be ruled out.
supporting_evidence: Spotting/pink tinge in urine possibly vaginal
LMP ~3 weeks ago – timing compatible with early gestation
opposing_evidence: Pain gradual rather than acute/severe typical of rupturing ectopic
No shoulder tip pain or syncope

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Lower-abdominal pain, systemic symptoms and inter-menstrual spotting in sexually active woman raise concern for PID.
opposing_evidence: No vaginal discharge or dyspareunia reported
Pain not clearly bilateral adnexal or worsened with movement
On implant which lowers but doesn’t eliminate PID risk

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Early appendicitis can present with periumbilical pain, nausea and fever; location currently diffuse below umbilicus without classic RLQ migration.
opposing_evidence: Pain not localized to right iliac fossa nor worsening over time
Normal bowel movements, no anorexia described

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: History of constipation last week could account for some discomfort, but bowels now regular and systemic symptoms less typical.
opposing_evidence: Subjective fever and nausea not explained by simple constipation
